rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; f8889 p. 1, line 14b; i8889 p. 8, Line 14b. Excess contributions withdrawn by the due date are refused by f8889.unsupported ("a withdrawal of excess contributions or their earnings, made in 2025 or in 2026 by the due date of your 2025 return, including extensions"), as the line's cite says, so on a completed return line 14b holds rollovers only.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i8889 p. 8, Line 15 ("Do not include the distribution of an excess contribution taken out after the due date, including extensions, of your return even if used for qualified medical expenses"). Any withdrawal of excess contributions made in 2025, and any earlier-year excess remaining in the HSA, is refused by f8889.unsupported, so the case cannot reach line 15 on a completed return.

rulings.restated: Input — Were any of your taxable HSA distributions made after you became disabled or turned age 65 (the exceptions to the additional 20% tax)?
rulings.model: The IRS exceptions are distributions made after the account beneficiary 'Dies, Becomes disabled or Turns age 65'; the restatement lists only disabled or age 65.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i8889 p. 9, Exceptions to the Additional 20% Tax ("distributions made after the account beneficiary: Dies, Becomes disabled or Turns age 65"). A distribution made after the account beneficiary's death is reported by the beneficiary or the estate; f8889.unsupported refuses "an HSA you acquired because of the account beneficiary's death" and "the HSA of a person who died in 2025 whose estate is the beneficiary", so only disability and age 65 can apply on a completed return.

rulings.model: For a filer not eligible every month who uses the last-month rule, the restatement uses a greater-of worksheet amount based on actual coverage changes; the IRS says 'You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month,' so the December 1 coverage amount governs.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change (owner ruling after Stage 11: keep rule 4). The model says that under the last-month rule the December 1 coverage amount governs (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2: "If the last-month rule (see Last-month rule, earlier) applies, you are considered an eligible individual for the entire year. You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year"); the restatement applies rule 4's greater-of when the coverage type changed (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 4: "If you were, or were considered, an eligible individual for the entire year and you changed your type of coverage during the year, enter on line 3 (see (6) in this list) the greater of: a. The limitation shown on the last line of the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet (in these instructions), or b. The maximum amount that can be contributed based on the type of HDHP coverage you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year"), the reading the owner chose because rule 4 names a filer who "were considered" eligible all year. The English states that reading accurately.

rulings.model: The IRS line says 'Enter the amount you and your employer contributed to your Archer MSAs for 2025 from Form 8853, lines 1 and 2' and to include spouse's Archer MSA contributions in family-coverage cases; the restatement always enters zero.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; f8889 p. 1, line 4: "Enter the amount you and your employer contributed to your Archer MSAs for 2025 from Form 8853, lines 1 and 2. If you or your spouse had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025, also include any amount contributed to your spouse's Archer MSAs". Every case with a nonzero line 4 is refused by f8889.unsupported, which since BUG-0236 asks about "contributions by you or your employer to an Archer MSA for 2025 (Form 8853), or, if you or your spouse had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025, any contribution by anyone to your spouse's Archer MSA"; the line's cite names the refusal. Zero is the value on every completed return.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; retain the already recorded owner choice amb.2025.hsa_line7_months (Owner accepted after Stage13). i8889 (2025) p.7 conditions mention family coverage, but p.5 Line3 Note removes the additional contribution amount from line3 for the entire year once a married filer has any family coverage. The register explicitly records both readings and chooses every eligible month, including self-only months, to avoid losing that part of the catch-up. The reviewer states the alternative literal reading; it is not classified as model error, newly human-approved, or an unrecorded change to the tax model.

rulings.model: The IRS worksheet counts months where 'You or your spouse had family coverage under an HDHP and were, or were considered to be, an eligible individual on the first day of the month,' but the program uses the general number of eligible months, overstating line 7 when family coverage exists only part of the year.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.hsa_line7_months (owner accepted after Stage 13). The model reads "number of months eligible" as only the months of family coverage and says the restatement overstates line 7 when family coverage did not last all year. i8889 p. 7, Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet: "1. $1,000 × number of months eligible"; the English states the project's chosen reading (every month treated as eligible) accurately. Under the model's reading the $1,000 for the self-only months would be lost, since i8889 p. 5, Line 3, Note says "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3", the register's reason. Same model reading as round 2.
